upstream.note: The newest published cmark-gfm release. It is pinned only as the implementation oracle for the GFM extension layer; current CommonMark semantics come from the separately pinned cmark release.

claim: The one Markdown Core dialect matches the pinned cmark-gfm GFM extension semantics except for the reviewed projections and exact divergences below. cmark-gfm has no authority over the CommonMark base or the additional dialect modules.

deltas.summary: An HTML comment is a `Comment` node whose literal is the bytes between `<!--` and `-->`: the inline token, and an HTML block that opens with `<!--` and whose end line holds only whitespace after the first `-->`. Upstream keeps both as html nodes holding the token as written.
deltas.handling: The shared normalizer maps upstream's comment nodes to `Comment` with the delimiters removed, which is the rule the engine applies on its own side (`docs/specs/dialect/comments.md`), and records that the projection acted. A model difference, so a projection rather than a list of inputs; the token and block boundaries are upstream's and are compared unchanged.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm removes unreferenced footnote definitions. Markdown Core keeps every valid definition as a document-owned `Footnote`, referenced or not.
deltas.rationale: An unreferenced definition is authored source and must remain represented. remark independently keeps it.
deltas.handling: The comparison projects Markdown Core's retained footnotes into cmark-gfm's resolved model before comparing.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm moves definitions to the document tail in reference order; Markdown Core's `Document.footnotes` holds them as values ordered by scope start.
deltas.handling: Both sides lift definitions into the same document-owned comparison order, preserving their content while ignoring the representation difference.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm derives a call label from neighbouring decoded nodes using source-column lengths. Markdown Core slices the authored source between brackets.
deltas.rationale: The upstream model loses bytes across line endings and can read a freed decode buffer when the caret came from an entity. A failed call must degrade to the bytes the author wrote.
deltas.handling: Exact inputs are registered because erasing labels globally would hide valid label differences.

deltas.summary: For nested duplicate definitions cmark-gfm keeps the one that closes first and destroys the other. Markdown Core resolves calls to the definition that opens first and retains the loser as a footnote after the winner, with the same id.
deltas.handling: The nested witness is registered exactly so the gate continues checking both resolution and retention.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm searches the whole line for `[x]`; Markdown Core reads only the marker the task-list scanner matched.
deltas.handling: The exact unchecked-item witness is registered. The completion projection preserves the false-versus-true difference caused by scanning a later literal [x].

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm can emit empty Text nodes after extension and break processing. Markdown Core and mdast omit nodes that own no source or content.
deltas.handling: The normalizer drops empty Text nodes on both sides and records that the projection acted.

deltas.summary: cmark-gfm flattens the already-parsed interior of an undefined footnote call. Markdown Core treats it as an unmatched bracket and preserves the CommonMark inline structure inside it.
deltas.rationale: An extension construct that did not resolve must not erase structure produced by the underlying language parser. remark agrees with Markdown Core.
deltas.handling: The emphasis and strikethrough witnesses are registered exactly.

deltas.summary: When a table is recovered from a multiline paragraph, cmark-gfm pipe-unescapes the split-off non-table lead twice. Markdown Core parses the lead once as an ordinary paragraph.
deltas.rationale: The lead is not table content; remark/micromark independently preserves the same spelling as Markdown Core.
deltas.handling: The escaped-pipe witness is registered exactly.

deltas.summary: The dialect's text directive claims a colon-led name, `:abc`, wherever the directives module admits one; CommonMark leaves the bytes as text.
deltas.rationale: The dialect index lists directives as a feature of the one language, judged by remark (`pnpm check:mdast-parity`), and remark-directive parses the same input to the same text directive.
deltas.handling: Keyed to the exact specification input.

deltas.summary: Boolean-only oracles retain task completion but lose the authored marker spelling, including x versus X.
deltas.handling: Compare the three shared states: absent, incomplete and complete. Exact marker spelling remains covered by canonical fixtures and binding tests; the non-leading [x] witness still compares unequal completion states.

deltas.summary: The canonical table stores head/content/foot groups and positive cell spans; pipe tables have one head row and unit spans.
deltas.handling: The oracle projection groups its first row as TableHead, its remaining rows as TableBody, and adds an empty TableFoot; cells gain rowspan=1 and colspan=1. Native table topology and spans are compared unchanged.
deltas.evidence: docs/specs/dialect/tables.md; canonical table fixtures and existing pipe-table oracle corpus.

deltas.summary: The task prefix is exactly one Unicode scalar plus SP, TAB, VT or FF, consumed once when any inherited list item opens, before deciding its first block. cmark-gfm only recognizes ASCII task states, misses quoted containers and can recognize later paragraphs.
deltas.handling: Exact module and historical fixture inputs pin custom markers, containers, opening-line ownership, block decisions and opaque bodies. No comparison erases task syntax.

deltas.summary: A single tilde is a subscript delimiter with non-empty, raw-whitespace-free content. Only a two-tilde run can be strikethrough; longer runs stay literal.
deltas.handling: The four historical single-tilde inputs remain in the corpus and are registered exactly. Product fixtures cover the complete P6 tilde and whitespace rules.

deltas.summary: The citations module recognizes @key at a valid Unicode word boundary and stores a typed bibliography Cite. The inherited base/GFM grammar has no bibliography citations.
deltas.handling: Retain exact changed inputs; citation keys, modes, affixes and scopes are covered by the Pandoc oracle and canonical conformance fixtures.

corpusNote: This gate intentionally does not compare unextended CommonMark examples. Markdown Core runs the `gfm` profile, which attaches the cmark-gfm extension set but leaves product directive and formula syntax disabled. CommonMark is checked separately against current cmark.
backlogNote: An entry here says cmark-gfm is right and this engine has not caught up yet. Each names the item that closes it and must still diverge until then; the commit that lands the fix deletes the entry, and `retiredBacklog` records only an entry whose input left the corpus without ever agreeing. scripts/check-upstream-parity.mjs enforces every direction.
